components.name: Primary Button
components.description: High-conversion primary CTA for contact booking and key hiring paths.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #58a6ff; color: #000000; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 14px 32px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s, background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #79b8ff; transform: scale(1.02); box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(88, 166, 255, 0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.95); }

components.name: Glass Button
components.description: Secondary action button with translucent glass effect and crisp border.
components.css: .ds-btn-glass { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); color: #ffffff; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 14px 32px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-glass:hover { border-color: rgba(88, 166, 255, 0.5); color: #58a6ff; background: rgba(88, 166, 255, 0.08); }

ARCHITECT

narrative.overview: The visual language marries the technical rigor and precision of an advanced developer IDE (subtle HUD grid lines, scanlines, monospace badges, terminal overlays) with the elegance and conversion clarity of a world-class digital product. Dark canvases provide a calm, distraction-free backdrop where vibrant electric accents and multi-theme palettes spotlight architecture case studies, metrics, and hiring paths.
keyCharacteristics: IDE-Inspired Atmosphere: Obsidian backdrops, terminal prompts, code-level badges, and custom theme switches.
Tactile Glass Layering: Translucent surfaces with calibrated backdrop blurs (8px to 24px) and luminous 1px perimeter borders.
Zero-Regret Performance: Visual enhancements defer until post-idle (html.fx-on) to keep FCP/LCP sub-second.
Dual Conversion & Proof Focus: Prominent CTA buttons with fluid hover states paired with real interactive engineering proof.

rules.name: The Rare Electric Accent Rule
rules.body: The primary electric accent is restricted to key interactive affordances, active states, and focal metrics (<=10% of any viewport). Its restraint commands instant visual priority.

rules.name: The Multi-Theme Invariant Rule
rules.body: Every color role must resolve dynamically through CSS custom properties (--primary, --background, --surface), allowing instant runtime switching between IDE presets without hardcoded overrides.

rules.name: The First-Paint System Font Rule
rules.body: First paint renders strictly with native local system font faces (ui-monospace, ui-sans-serif) to eliminate layout shifts and network blocking. Webfonts load asynchronously and hydrate smoothly after load.

rules.name: The Glass Blur Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Mobile viewports compute lightweight backdrop blurs (8px), while desktop viewports receive deep blurs (20px - 24px), preventing mobile GPU rendering bottlenecks.

rules.name: The No-Double-Blur Rule
rules.body: Nested containers within a glass card must use .glass-lite or .surface-utility (zero extra blur) to prevent stacking multiple heavy blur layers.

dos: Do use semantic CSS variables (var(--primary), var(--background)) for every visual property to guarantee complete multi-theme support.
Do preserve 44px minimum touch targets on all mobile interactive elements.
Do test high contrast (4.5:1 text-to-background ratio) across both Dark Modern and Tokyo Night themes.
Do use .glass-lite on nested cards inside glass containers to keep frame rates at 60fps.
donts: Don't hardcode static hex colors in component templates when a theme token exists.
Don't apply heavy drop shadows without a glass border; dark themes require luminous border contours for boundary definition.
Don't load render-blocking webfonts on initial paint; let the local system stack render FCP instantly.
Don't crowd the screen with neon accents; reserve {colors.primary} for focused interactive elements.
